title: Hotels and restaurants
subtitle: book a room in advance, check in, a three-course meal
summary: Book and describe a hotel room, and order a meal in a restaurant in natural English.

lesson.heading: Hotel facilities
rows: staff bring food and drink to your room
a system that keeps the air cool
TV with many channels from different countries
a small fridge in your room
a box to keep money and valuable items in
lesson.note: The hotel is in the heart of Paris. heart = centre.

lesson.heading: Types of room
rows: two people, with one big bed

lesson.heading: Staying in a hotel
lesson.text: Rooms are often **available** during the week, but many hotels are **fully booked** at weekends. So you may need to **book a room in advance**. When you arrive, you **check in** at **reception**; at the end of your **stay** you **check out**.

examples.text: You normally have to **check out** by midday.

lesson.heading: Going to a restaurant
lesson.text: At the weekend it is a good idea to **book a table** or **make a reservation**. Many restaurants offer **three-course meals** with a **starter** (e.g. soup), a **main course** (e.g. meat or fish) and a **dessert** (e.g. fruit with ice cream).

examples.text: If service isn't included, it's normal to leave a **tip**.
examples.note: a tip = extra money you give to the waiter

lesson.heading: Ordering a meal
lesson.text: The waiter asks **Are you ready to order?** You answer with **I'd like ...** or **I'll have ...**. For a steak the waiter asks **How would you like your steak?** - **rare**, **medium** or **well-done**. For water, **still** or **sparkling**.

examples.text: I'd like to start with the spicy prawns, and then **I'll have** the fillet steak.

lesson.text: In a restaurant say *I'll have the steak*, never ~~I take the steak~~.

exercises.prompt: Put each word in the correct group.
Match the words on the left with the words on the right.
Two friends want a room with two separate beds. Which room do they book?
exercises.explanation: A twin room has two beds; a double room has one big bed.

exercises.prompt: Could you first check in at ___, please? They will give you your key.
exercises.explanation: You check in at reception and get your room key.

exercises.prompt: I ___ the soup, and then the fish for my main course.
exercises.explanation: In a restaurant we order with I'll have ..., not ~~I take ...~~

exercises.prompt: Service wasn't included, so I left a 10% ___.
exercises.explanation: A tip is extra money you give to the waiter or waitress.

exercises.prompt: The hotel is in the ___ of the town, close to all the main attractions.
exercises.explanation: in the heart of = in the centre of.

exercises.prompt: At the end of your ___ at a hotel, you normally have to check out by midday.
exercises.hint: (the time you spend in a place)
exercises.explanation: Your stay is the period of time you spend in a place.

exercises.prompt: Did you book a table? = Did you make a ___?
exercises.explanation: make a reservation = book a table.

exercises.prompt: The hotel was fully booked. = There were no rooms ___.
exercises.explanation: If a room is available, you can find one; if the hotel is fully booked, all the rooms are taken.

exercises.prompt: Did you book it before you went? = Did you book it in ___?

exercises.statement: The waiter asks what you want, and you say: 'I take the steak, please.'
exercises.explanation: I'll have the steak, please. We do not say ~~I take the steak~~.

exercises.prompt: The waiter wants to know if you want your steak rare, medium or well-done. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: How would you like your steak?
exercises.explanation: The answer is Rare, medium or well-done.
